saints.name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: The “Lily of the Mohawks,” a young Mohawk-Algonquin convert of New France whose purity and penance shone amid great opposition, and the first Native American…
biography: Kateri Tekakwitha was born in 1656 at Ossernenon, in the Mohawk country of what is now upstate New York, the daughter of a Mohawk chief and a Christian Algonquin mother. Smallpox in her childhood killed her parents and left her face scarred and her eyesight weak. She was baptized by the Jesuit missionary Jacques de Lamberville on Easter of 1676.

For her faith she met scorn and threats from her own people, and about 1677 she fled some two hundred miles to the Christian mission of Kahnawake, near Montreal. There she gave herself to prayer, penance, and the care of the sick and aged, taking a vow of perpetual virginity. She died on 17 April 1680; witnesses reported that the scars vanished from her face soon after death.
saints.knownFor: Heroic purity, penance, and constancy under persecution among the Mohawk of New France.

canonization.canonized: 2012 by Pope Benedict XVI — the first Native American saint

sources.text: USCCB liturgical calendar — optional memorial, 14 July (USA); the general Roman calendar keeps her on 17 April
